definition_zh: 抓住；接住；赶上；染上；听懂
definition_en: to take hold of something moving, to reach a bus or train in time, to get an illness, or to hear and understand something
core_image: 伸手一扑，把正在动的东西按在手里
scene: 球场上队友把球高高抛起。He jumped and caught the ball with one hand.
sceneCN: 这里 catch 指「接住」（第 1 个义项：用手抓住运动中的东西）；句意是他跳起来，单手接住了球。

pos.zh: 抓住；接住；赶上；染上；听懂

senses.title: To take hold of something moving
senses.definition: to stop and hold a moving object with the hands
senses.definitionCN: 用手拦住并握住运动中的物体
senses.example: She caught the keys he threw her.
senses.exampleCN: 她接住了他扔来的钥匙。
senses.why: The core image is a hand closing on something in flight, and that is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一只手合拢在飞行中的东西上，这也是最古老的义项。

senses.title: To reach a bus or train in time
senses.definition: to arrive early enough to get on a bus, train, plane or boat
senses.definitionCN: 到得够早，能登上公交、火车、飞机或船
senses.example: We ran and caught the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们跑着赶上了末班车。
senses.why: A departing vehicle is a moving target, so boarding it in time is catching it.
senses.whyCN: 开走的车就是一个移动目标，及时登上它也就是「抓住」它。

senses.title: To get an illness
senses.definition: to become infected with a disease or pick up an illness from others
senses.definitionCN: 被疾病感染，或从他人那里染上病
senses.example: He caught a cold after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行之后他感冒了。
senses.why: An illness is pictured as something passing by that the body seizes.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被想象成从身边经过、被身体抓住的东西。

senses.title: To hear and understand
senses.definition: to manage to hear words or understand a joke or meaning
senses.definitionCN: 设法听清话语，或理解笑话与含义
senses.example: I did not catch what she said.
senses.exampleCN: 我没听清她说什么。
senses.why: Understanding is pictured as grabbing hold of words before they fly away.
senses.whyCN: 理解被想象成在话语飞走之前把它抓住。

intro.en: Catch came through northern French from a Latin verb meaning to try to seize, and its spelling kept the French sound.
intro.cn: catch 经法国北部方言上溯到拉丁语中意为试图抓取的动词，拼写保留了法语读音。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and captare meant to keep trying to seize.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为拿取，captare 意为反复试图抓取。

items.en: Cachier meant to chase or hunt, a northern French form of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 古北法语 cachier 意为追捕，是拉丁语动词的北部方言形式。

items.en: Cacchen appears in the thirteenth century for chasing and seizing.
items.cn: 中古英语 cacchen 在十三世纪已指追逐与抓取。

items.en: The word extends to catching a train, catching cold and catching meaning.
items.cn: 此后词义扩展到赶车、受凉和听懂意思。

items.en: Modern idioms add catch fire, catch sight of and catch up with.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上着火、瞥见和追上等习语。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the English family of catch, while the meaning group lists other verbs for seizing.
note.cn: 形近组沿 catch 的英语词族展开，近义组列出其他表示抓取的动词。

entries.definition: a person or thing that catches
able to spread from person to person
entries.definitionCN: 能在人与人之间传染的

entries.definition: easy to remember and repeat
to take hold of something suddenly and firmly
to take something quickly with the hand
to take a person or animal prisoner

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie catch to its Latin seize root, to the irregular past caught and to common idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 catch 与拉丁语抓取词根、不规则过去式 caught 以及常见习语连起来。

normal.en: Catch and capture share the Latin root cap, to take, which explains why both mean seizing.
normal.cn: catch 与 capture 共享拉丁语词根 cap（拿取），这解释了为什么两者都表示抓。

normal.en: The past tense is caught, rhyming with taught and bought, all old irregular forms.
normal.cn: 过去式是 caught，与 taught、bought 押韵，都是古老的不规则形式。

normal.en: Catch a cold pictures the illness as a passing object you grab.
normal.cn: catch a cold 把疾病想象成一个路过、被你抓住的东西。

normal.en: Catch a train keeps the same move: you reach the departing vehicle in time.
normal.cn: catch a train 保留同一动作：你及时够到了正在离开的车。

normal.en: Catchy music is music that catches in your head and will not leave.
normal.cn: catchy 的音乐就是抓住你脑子、赶不走的音乐。

abstract.en: Picture a hand snapping shut around a thrown ball.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手啪地合拢，扣住飞来的球。

abstract.en: Picture a runner sliding through closing train doors.
abstract.cn: 想象奔跑者从正在合拢的车门间挤进去。

abstract.en: Picture a word flying past and being snatched out of the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词从耳边飞过，被凌空抓下。

examples.en: Can you catch the ball with your left hand?
examples.cn: 你能用左手接住球吗？

examples.en: I need to catch the early train tomorrow.
examples.cn: 我明天得赶早班火车。

examples.en: She caught a cold during the trip.
examples.cn: 她在旅途中感冒了。

dict_mnemonic.text: catch 短促有力，像手掌「咔」一下合上：抓住球、抓住车、抓住病、抓住话里的意思。

root: 源自古北法语 cachier（追捕），上溯拉丁语 captare（反复试图抓取），是 capere（拿取）的反复形式。

sensesIntro.en: One snatching gesture extends to vehicles, illnesses and words, because all of them are things that pass and can be seized.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个抓取动作扩展到车、病和话，因为它们都是经过身边、可以被抓住的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on something in motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢在运动中的东西上。

branches.en: The literal hand closes on a ball, a rope or a key.
branches.cn: 字面义是手合拢在球、绳或钥匙上。

branches.en: A departing vehicle is caught by arriving in time.
branches.cn: 开走的车靠及时赶到而被「抓住」。

branches.en: An illness is caught as it passes through the air.
branches.cn: 疾病像从空气里经过时被抓住。

branches.en: Meaning is caught when the words are held long enough to be understood.
branches.cn: 话语被握住足够久、听明白了，意思就被抓住。

branches.en: Both depend on speed and timing rather than strength.
branches.cn: 两者都取决于速度和时机，而非力量。

intro.en: Catch forms agent and adjective nouns with -er, -ing and -y, and keeps an irregular past.
intro.cn: catch 用 -er、-ing、-y 构成名词与形容词，并保留不规则过去式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base capere, to take, is the same root behind capture, captive and accept.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 capere（拿取）也是 capture、captive 与 accept 的词根。

items.example: She catches every cold going round.
items.exampleCN: 流行什么感冒她都染上。

items.example: They caught the thief at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 他们在大门口抓住了小偷。

items.meaning: spreading, or in the act of seizing
items.meaningCN: 有传染性的，或正在抓取

items.example: The catcher signalled for a fast ball.
The song has a catchy chorus.
Captare is the source of catch.
items.exampleCN: captare 是 catch 的来源。
capere 也是 capture 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Capere is the base of many English words.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capere 是许多英语词的词基。
captare 传入了法国北部方言。

definition_zh: adj. 明确无疑的，绝对的；范畴的，分类的
definition_en: stated in a direct and certain way, with no doubt allowed; relating to categories
core_image: 一句话斩钉截铁，不留余地
scene: 发言人明确表示，这类请求一律拒绝。The spokesman gave a categorical refusal of every such request.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：categorical 指明确无疑的；句意是发言人一口拒绝所有这类请求。

senses.title: Said without doubt
senses.definition: expressed clearly and with no possibility of exception
senses.definitionCN: 表达清楚，不允许任何例外
senses.example: The minister issued a categorical denial.
senses.exampleCN: 部长断然否认。
senses.why: The word came from Greek kategorikos, said of a statement, from kategorein, to assert.
senses.whyCN: 该词源自希腊语 kategorikos（关于陈述的），来自 kategorein（断言）。

senses.title: Of categories
senses.definition: relating to a class or to logical categories
senses.definitionCN: 与类别或逻辑范畴有关的
senses.example: The two claims are categorical rather than historical.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个主张属于范畴层面而非历史层面。
senses.why: Philosophy kept the older sense of naming and classifying.
senses.whyCN: 哲学保留了命名与分类的旧义。

intro.en: Categorical comes from Greek kategorikos, from kategorein, to assert or accuse in public.
intro.cn: categorical 源自希腊语 kategorikos，来自 kategorein（公开断言或指控）。

items.en: Kategorein means to assert in public.
items.cn: kategorein 意为公开断言。

items.en: Kategoria names a class or a statement.
items.cn: kategoria 指类别或陈述。

items.en: Logic borrows categorical for direct statements.
items.cn: 十五世纪逻辑学用 categorical 指直接陈述。

items.en: Kant names the categorical imperative.
items.cn: 十八世纪康德提出绝对命令。

items.en: Everyday speech keeps the sense of no doubt.
items.cn: 现代日常用法保留毫无疑问义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the categor- stem; the near-meaning group separates firm statements from cautious ones.
note.cn: 形近组共享 categor- 词干；近义组区分坚定陈述与谨慎表述。

entries.definition: A class of things.
To place things in classes.
A shorter adjective form.
Complete and without limit.
Not limited by conditions.
Said with force.

normalIntro.en: A categorical answer is one filed under no exceptions.
normalIntro.cn: categorical 的回答会被归入没有例外这一类别。

normal.en: Kategoria meant a class.
normal.cn: kategoria 指类别。

normal.en: Logic used it for direct statements.
normal.cn: 逻辑学用它指直接陈述。

normal.en: A categorical denial leaves no room.
normal.cn: 断然否认不留余地。

normal.en: Kant made the imperative famous.
normal.cn: 康德让绝对命令广为人知。

normal.en: The adjective keeps both senses.
normal.cn: 这个形容词兼有两种含义。

abstract.en: A door closed with one clean click.
abstract.cn: 一声干脆落锁的门。

abstract.en: A sentence with no back door.
abstract.cn: 一句没有后门的话。

abstract.en: A label that forbids relabelling.
abstract.cn: 禁止再贴标签的标签。

examples.en: The minister issued a categorical denial.
examples.cn: 部长发表了断然否认。

examples.en: He was categorical about the deadline.
examples.cn: 他对截止期限说得斩钉截铁。

examples.en: She categorically denied the charge.
examples.cn: 她断然否认了这项指控。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡台哥瑞扣」——把话卡在台面上，一锤定音，绝不改口。

root: 希腊语 kategorein（公开断言）→ kategorikos → 英语 categorical

sensesIntro.en: Asserting and classifying are the same old word seen from two angles.
sensesIntro.cn: 断言与分类，是同一个古老词语的两个侧面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence nailed flat to the table
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话被钉平在桌面上

branches.en: A refusal that ends the discussion.
branches.cn: 一句结束讨论的拒绝。

branches.en: A promise with no conditions.
branches.cn: 一个没有条件的承诺。

branches.en: A claim about kinds, not cases.
branches.cn: 关于类别而非个案的论断。

branches.en: A philosopher sorting predicates.
branches.cn: 哲学家整理谓词。

branches.en: Certainty organised into classes.
branches.cn: 被整理进类别的确定性。

intro.en: Categorical carries a Greek root; the list below adds words for speech, logic and classes.
intro.cn: categorical 带有希腊词根；下面列出言语、逻辑、类别词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek kategorein is to assert, and Latin dicere is to say.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kategorein 意为断言，拉丁语 dicere 意为说。

latinEntries.exampleCN: kategoria 产生 category 与 categorical。
dicere 产生 dictate 与 verdict。
classis 产生 class 与 classify。

definition_zh: 类别；种类；范畴
definition_en: a group of people or things that share a particular quality, or a basic class in philosophy and logic
core_image: 把一大堆东西分进贴着标签的格子
scene: 评委把参赛作品分成几组。Each entry was placed in a different category.
sceneCN: 这里 category 指「类别」（第 1 个义项：按共同特点划分的一组）；句意是每件参赛作品都被归入不同的类别。

senses.title: A class of similar things
senses.definition: a group of people or things that share a common feature and are treated together
senses.definitionCN: 具有共同特点、被放在一起处理的一组人或物
senses.example: These films belong to the same category.
senses.exampleCN: 这些影片属于同一类别。
senses.why: The Greek word was a public statement about what something is, and naming a class is exactly that kind of statement.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源词是对某物是什么的公开断言，而给一个类别命名正是这种断言。

senses.title: A basic class in logic
senses.definition: one of the most general classes used to analyse reality, such as quantity, quality or relation
senses.definitionCN: 用于分析现实的最普遍类别，如数量、性质或关系
senses.example: Kant listed twelve categories of understanding.
senses.exampleCN: 康德列出了十二个知性范畴。
senses.why: Philosophy takes the everyday class word and raises it to the widest possible divisions of thought.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常的类别词提升为思维中最宽泛的划分。

intro.en: Category began as a Greek word for a public accusation, then became the logical term for what can be stated of a thing.
intro.cn: category 最初是希腊语中公开指控的说法，后来成为逻辑学中「关于某物能说什么」的术语。

items.en: Agora was the public assembly, and agoreuein meant to speak in public.
items.cn: 希腊语 agora 指公民大会，agoreuein 意为当众发言。

items.en: Kategoria meant an accusation, a statement made publicly against someone.
items.cn: kategoria 意为指控，即当众针对某人作出的陈述。

items.en: Aristotle used the word for the basic ways something can be predicated, such as quantity or relation.
items.cn: 亚里士多德用该词指述说某物的基本方式，如数量或关系。

items.en: Categoria was borrowed into Latin as a technical term of logic.
items.cn: categoria 作为逻辑学术语被借入拉丁语。

items.en: French categorie carried the logical term into ordinary classification.
items.cn: 法语 categorie 把这个逻辑术语带入日常分类。

items.en: Modern English uses category for any practical grouping, from age groups to product types.
items.cn: 现代英语用 category 指任何实用分组，从年龄组到产品类型。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the classify family, while the meaning group gives other grouping words.
note.cn: 形近组沿分类词族展开，近义组给出其他表示分组的词。

entries.definition: to put things into classes
the act of sorting into classes
stated without conditions or doubt
entries.definitionCN: 无条件、毫不含糊地陈述的

entries.definition: a group of things of the same kind
a kind or sort of person or thing
a set of people or things placed together
entries.definitionCN: 放在一起的一组人或物

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the public-speech root, the -ize and -ical family and the everyday grouping phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「当众发言」词根、-ize 与 -ical 词族以及日常分组搭配。

normal.en: Category and categorize differ by the -ize ending, which turns the class into an action.
normal.cn: category 与 categorize 只差 -ize 词尾，后者把类别变成动作。

normal.en: The Greek root agora, a public square, also appears in agoraphobia, fear of open spaces.
normal.cn: 希腊语词根 agora（公共广场）也出现在 agoraphobia（广场恐惧）里。

normal.en: Age category and product category show the word doing practical sorting work.
normal.cn: age category 与 product category 展示这个词的实际分组功能。

normal.en: Categorical answers leave no room for doubt, as if the class were fixed for ever.
normal.cn: categorical 的回答不留怀疑余地，仿佛类别已经永久定死。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies, so one category becomes many categories.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变成 ies，一个 category 变成许多 categories。

abstract.en: Picture a market square where a speaker names each item aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象集市广场上有人高声给每样东西归类。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of labelled drawers, each holding one kind of thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一面贴着标签的抽屉墙，每格只放一类东西。

abstract.en: Picture a judge sorting cards into neat piles on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判在桌上把卡片分成整齐的几堆。

examples.en: The prize has a separate category for young writers.
examples.cn: 该奖项为年轻作者单设一个类别。

examples.en: Books in this category sell quickly.
examples.cn: 这一类别的书卖得很快。

examples.en: Please categorize the files by date.
examples.cn: 请按日期把文件分类。

dict_mnemonic.text: category 里有 cate 加 gory：想象把东西按标签排成一排排格子，每一格就是一个类别。

root: 源自希腊语 kategoria（公开指控、断言），由 kata（针对）与 agoreuein（当众发言）构成，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A public statement about what something is becomes a logical class, then any practical grouping of things.
sensesIntro.cn: 关于某物是什么的公开断言变成逻辑类别，再变成任何实用的分组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled slot into which similar things are sorted.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个贴着标签、用来归放同类物的格子。

branches.en: Philosophy keeps the widest classes of predication.
branches.cn: 哲学保留了最宽泛的述谓类别。

branches.en: Everyday use narrows the class to any group sharing a feature.
branches.cn: 日常用法把类别收窄为任何共享某一特点的组。

branches.en: Age category and product category apply the grouping to people and goods.
branches.cn: 年龄组与产品类别把分组用到人和货物上。

branches.en: Both senses answer the question of what kind of thing something is.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在回答「这属于哪一种东西」。

branches.en: The logical sense stays technical and mostly appears in philosophy.
branches.cn: 逻辑义偏技术性，多出现在哲学文本中。

intro.en: Category builds verbs and nouns with -ize and -ization, and an adjective with -ical.
intro.cn: category 用 -ize、-ization 构成动词与名词，用 -ical 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin categoria preserved the Greek term of logic, which French later passed to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 categoria 保留了希腊语逻辑术语，法语后来把它传给英语。

items.exampleCN: kategoria 经亚里士多德进入逻辑学。
agora 藏在 kategoria 之中。

latinEntries.example: Categoria passed from Greek into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: categoria 从希腊语进入拉丁语。

definition_zh: v. 为活动提供饮食；迎合，满足需要
definition_en: to provide food and drink for an event; to give people what they want or need
core_image: 一队人推着餐车走进会场
scene: 这家小公司为婚礼提供餐饮，也按客人的口味调整菜单。The small firm caters for weddings and adjusts the menu to every taste.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cater 指提供饮食；句意是这家公司为婚礼供餐并按口味调整菜单。

senses.title: Feeding an event
senses.definition: to supply food and drink for a group or occasion
senses.definitionCN: 为群体或活动供应饮食
senses.example: They catered the whole conference.
senses.exampleCN: 整场会议由他们供餐。
senses.why: The word came from Anglo-French acater, to buy provisions.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自盎格鲁-法语 acater（采买食物）。

senses.title: Meeting a need
senses.definition: to provide what a group wants or needs
senses.definitionCN: 提供某群体想要或需要的东西
senses.example: The course caters to beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课照顾初学者。
senses.why: The buying sense widened to supplying any demand.
senses.whyCN: 采买义扩展到满足任何需求。

intro.en: Cater comes from Anglo-French acater, to buy provisions, and first meant to act as a buyer of food.
intro.cn: cater 来自盎格鲁-法语 acater（采买食物），最初指充当食物采买人。

items.en: Anglo-French acater means to buy provisions.
items.cn: 十四世纪盎格鲁-法语 acater 意为采买食物。

items.en: English cater means to provide food.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语 cater 意为供应食物。

items.en: A caterer supplies banquets and inns.
items.cn: 十七世纪 caterer 为宴席与客栈供货。

definition_zh: 因果性；因果律；因果关系；因果作用
definition_en: the principle or property by which causes produce effects, or the quality of being causal
core_image: 一张看不见的网：每个节点都连着前一个节点，整张网就是因果性
scene: 哲学导论课上，老师在黑板上写下原因、因果作用、因果性三个词，然后提问。In the philosophy class, the teacher writes cause, causation and causality on the board and asks which one names the principle itself.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：causality 指因果性、因果律；句意是老师在黑板上写下三个词，问哪一个命名了原则本身。

pos.zh: 因果性；因果律；因果关系

forms.label: 复数（多种因果体系，较少用）

senses.title: The property of being causal
senses.definition: the quality that makes one thing able to produce another
senses.definitionCN: 使一物能够产生另一物的性质
senses.example: Philosophers debate whether causality belongs to things or to our descriptions of them.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家争论因果性属于事物本身，还是属于我们对事物的描述。
senses.why: The suffix -ity turns an adjective into a property. Causality is not a particular cause or a particular link, but the quality of being causal at all.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ity 把形容词变成属性。causality 不是某个原因或某条连接，而是“具有因果性”这一性质本身。

senses.title: The principle that every event has a cause
senses.titleCN: 每个事件都有原因的原则
senses.definition: the principle that nothing happens without a cause, often treated as a law of thought or of nature
senses.definitionCN: 没有事物无缘无故发生的原则，常被视为思维或自然的法则
senses.example: Kant treated causality as a category of the understanding.
senses.exampleCN: 康德把因果性视为知性的一个范畴。
senses.why: Philosophy made the property into a principle. Once stated as a law, causality governs all events rather than describing one link.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把属性变成原则。一旦被陈述为法则，因果性就支配一切事件，而不是描述某一条连接。

senses.title: Cause and effect taken together
senses.titleCN: 原因与结果的总体关系
senses.definition: the whole system of cause-effect relations, considered as one subject
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个整体主题来考察的全部因果关系系统
senses.example: The book studies causality in complex systems.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书研究复杂系统中的因果关系。
senses.why: This is the collective use: not one arrow but the whole network. It is close to causation, but wider and more abstract.
senses.whyCN: 这是集合用法：不是一支箭头，而是整张网。它接近 causation，但更宽、更抽象。

senses.title: A philosophical category
senses.definition: in philosophy, one of the basic categories through which the mind organises experience
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中心智借以组织经验的基本范畴之一
senses.example: The critique asks whether causality is a feature of the world or of thought.
senses.exampleCN: 这项批判追问因果性是世界的特征，还是思维的特征。
senses.why: Kant's move made causality a form imposed by the mind. The word then names a condition of possible experience, not an observable relation.
senses.whyCN: 康德的做法把因果性变成心智施加的形式。这个词于是命名可能经验的条件，而不是可观察的关系。

senses.title: Deterministic chains of causes
senses.definition: the view or situation in which every later state follows necessarily from earlier ones
senses.definitionCN: 每个后续状态都必然由先前状态得出的观点或情形
senses.example: Laplace imagined a mind that could predict everything through causality.
senses.exampleCN: 拉普拉斯想象了一种能通过因果性预测一切的心智。
senses.why: If causality is a universal law, the whole future is a chain. The word then carries a determinist weight that everyday 'cause' does not.
senses.whyCN: 如果因果性是普遍法则，整个未来就是一条链。这个词于是带上决定论的分量，而日常的 cause 没有这层分量。

senses.title: Causality in scientific research
senses.definition: the property that a study tries to establish when it moves beyond association
senses.definitionCN: 研究在超越关联时试图确立的那种性质
senses.example: The review graded the causality of each reported side effect.
senses.exampleCN: 这项综述对报告的每种副作用进行了因果性分级。
senses.why: Science uses the word when it must decide whether a observed association deserves the name of causation. Causality is the target, not the starting point.
senses.whyCN: 科学在必须判断某种观察到的关联是否配得上“因果”之名时使用这个词。因果性是目标，而不是起点。

senses.title: Legal causality
senses.definition: the degree to which an act can be treated as the cause of a legally relevant result
senses.definitionCN: 某一行为可被视为法律相关结果之原因的程度
senses.example: The judgment separates factual from legal causality.
senses.exampleCN: 该判决把事实因果性与法律因果性分开。
senses.why: Law adds a normative layer: not every link in the chain counts for liability. Causality here is a property the court is willing to recognise, not merely a physical fact.
senses.whyCN: 法律加上了一层规范：并非链上的每条连接都算作责任。这里的因果性是法院愿意承认的属性，而不只是物理事实。

senses.title: Narrative causality
senses.definition: in literary criticism, the way a story connects events so that one seems to lead to the next
senses.definitionCN: 文学批评中故事连接事件、使前事看似引出后事的方式
senses.example: The novel's causality is emotional rather than logical.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的因果性是情感的，而不是逻辑的。
senses.why: Stories need events to feel caused even when no physical cause exists. Criticism borrowed the word to describe that invented connective tissue.
senses.whyCN: 故事需要事件显得有原因，即使并不存在物理原因。批评界借用这个词来描述这种被发明出来的连接组织。

senses.title: The intuition of causality
senses.definition: in psychology, the human tendency to perceive certain events as causing others
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中人类把某些事件感知为造成另一些事件的倾向
senses.example: Infants appear to develop an intuition of causality early.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿似乎很早就发展出因果直觉。
senses.why: Psychology locates causality in the perceiver. The word now names a habit of the mind, which is exactly the point Hume made about the relation itself.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把因果性定位在感知者身上。这个词现在命名心智的一种习惯，而这正是休谟对因果关系本身所做的论断。

intro.en: Causality is a scholastic abstraction: Latin causalitas, built on causalis with the abstract suffix -itas. It entered English philosophy as the name of a property or principle, which is why it sounds more theoretical than causation.
intro.cn: causality 是一个经院哲学式的抽象词：拉丁语 causalitas，由 causalis 加抽象后缀 -itas 构成。它作为属性或原则的名称进入英语哲学，因此听起来比 causation 更理论化。

items.en: Causa supplied the whole family: cause, causal, causation and causality. Its range included 'reason', 'motive' and 'legal case', so the descendants split along those lines.
items.cn: causa 提供了整个词族：cause、causal、causation、causality。它的范围包括“理由”“动机”“法律案件”，后代词便沿着这些线分化。

items.en: Causalis, 'of a cause', was the adjective used by Latin writers on philosophy and grammar. English borrowed it almost unchanged as causal.
items.cn: causalis“原因的”是拉丁哲学与语法作家使用的形容词。英语几乎原样借入作 causal。

items.en: Causalitas was formed with -itas, the abstract suffix that gives English -ity. Scholastic writers used it for the property of being a cause, a term of analysis rather than of everyday speech.
items.cn: causalitas 由 -itas 构成，这个抽象后缀对应英语 -ity。经院作家用它指“作为原因的性质”，这是分析术语，不是日常言语。

items.en: English causality appears in philosophical writing in the 17th century, alongside causal and causation. The three words were differentiated by part of speech and by level of abstraction.
items.cn: 英语 causality 在 17 世纪与 causal、causation 一同出现在哲学写作中。这三个词按词性与抽象层级被区分开来。

items.en: Hume analysed causality as a habit of expectation, and Kant rebuilt it as a category of the understanding. The word became a battlefield term in epistemology.
items.cn: 休谟把因果性分析为一种期待的习惯，康德则把它重建为知性的范畴。这个词成了认识论的战场术语。

items.en: Science added causality assessment, reverse causality and multicausality. Literary criticism added narrative causality. The word now names a property to be tested, denied or narrated.
items.cn: 科学增加了因果性评估、反向因果与多因性。文学批评增加了叙事因果性。这个词现在命名一种可被检验、否认或叙述的属性。

note.en: Causality, causation and causal are a closely related trio, and casualty is a dangerous look-alike from a different root. The groups sort both problems.
note.cn: causality、causation、causal 是关系很近的三件套，而 casualty 是来自另一词根的危险形近词。两组分别处理这两个问题。

entries.definition: a person killed or injured in an accident or war. It comes from Latin casus 'a fall', not from causa, and has nothing to do with causes.
entries.definitionCN: 事故或战争中伤亡的人。它来自拉丁语 casus“落下”，不是 causa，与原因无关。

entries.definition: the relation between a cause and its effect. Causality is the general property or principle; causation is the particular relation.
entries.definitionCN: 因与果之间的关系。causality 是普遍属性或原则，causation 是具体关系。

entries.definition: relating to a cause. It is the adjective of the family, while causality is the abstract noun.
entries.definitionCN: 与原因有关的。它是词族中的形容词，而 causality 是抽象名词。

entries.definition: the doctrine that every event is fixed by prior conditions. Causality alone does not require this strong claim.
entries.definitionCN: 主张每个事件都由先前条件固定的学说。单凭因果性并不需要这么强的主张。

entries.definition: a mutual variation of quantities. It is what causality is often wrongly reduced to.
entries.definitionCN: 数量之间的相互变化。它常被错误地还原为因果性。

entries.definition: the quality of being impossible to be otherwise. Some theories of causality include necessity, others do not.
entries.definitionCN: 不可能不是如此的性质。有些因果理论包含必然性，有些则不含。

entries.definition: the capacity to act and produce effects. It locates causality in an actor rather than in a law.
entries.definitionCN: 行动并产生效果的能力。它把因果性定位在行动者，而不是法则中。

normalIntro.en: These hooks separate the -ity abstraction from the -tion relation, and mark the casualty trap.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 -ity 的抽象与 -tion 的关系分开，并标出 casualty 这个陷阱。

normal.en: See the suffix: causal + -ity makes a property, not a single link.
normal.cn: 看见后缀：causal 加 -ity 造出属性，而不是单条连接。

normal.en: Keep the trio: cause is the thing, causation is the link, causality is the principle.
normal.cn: 记住三件套：cause 是事物，causation 是连接，causality 是原则。

normal.en: Watch the trap: casualty is a victim, not a principle. One letter changes the whole family.
normal.cn: 当心陷阱：casualty 是伤亡者，不是原则。一个字母换掉整个词族。

normal.en: Use the phrase principle of causality for the philosophical sense.
normal.cn: 哲学义用 principle of causality 这一说法。

normal.en: In research, pair causality with assessment and reverse causality.
normal.cn: 在研究语境中，把 causality 与 assessment、reverse causality 配对。

abstract.en: Hold one network, not one arrow: causality is the whole web of arrows.
abstract.cn: 抓住一张网，而不是一支箭头：causality 是全部箭头的网。

abstract.en: Sort the senses by discipline: philosophy, science, law, literature, psychology.
abstract.cn: 按学科分组义项：哲学、科学、法律、文学、心理学。

abstract.en: Remember the abstraction ladder: cause, causal, causation, causality.
abstract.cn: 记住抽象阶梯：cause、causal、causation、causality。

examples.en: The principle of causality states that every event has a cause.
examples.cn: 因果律原则指出每个事件都有原因。

examples.en: The study could not rule out reverse causality.
examples.cn: 这项研究无法排除反向因果。

examples.en: Literary critics speak of narrative causality when plot events feel inevitable.
examples.cn: 当情节事件显得必然时，文学批评家会谈及叙事因果性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“烤杂了题”：把各种原因“烤”在一起，成一整套“题”——causality 就是因果性。注意别读成 casualty 伤亡者。

root: 拉丁语 causa“原因”加后缀构成 causalis“原因的”，再加抽象后缀 -itas 成晚期拉丁语 causalitas“因果性”；英语经哲学写作借入作 causality。与 casus“落下”派生的 casualty 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Causality is the abstract member of the family: not a cause, not one link, but the property or principle that makes links possible. Philosophy treats it as a law or a category, science as a property to be established, law as a limit on responsibility, and literature as an effect the story must create.
sensesIntro.cn: causality 是词族中最抽象的成员：不是原因，不是某条连接，而是使连接成为可能的属性或原则。哲学把它当作法则或范畴，科学把它当作待确立的属性，法律把它当作责任的界限，文学把它当作故事必须制造出的效果。

core.en: The quality behind all arrows: whatever makes one thing able to produce another.
core.cn: 一切箭头背后的性质：使一物能够产生另一物的东西。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY: being causal, and the whole network of relations.
branches.cn: 属性：具有因果性，以及全部关系网。

branches.en: THE PRINCIPLE: a law of nature, a category of mind, and a determinist chain.
branches.cn: 原则：自然法则、心智范畴，以及决定论链条。

branches.en: THE TEST: scientific assessment and legal attribution.
branches.cn: 检验：科学评估与法律归责。

branches.en: THE STORY: causality manufactured by narrative.
branches.cn: 故事：由叙事制造出来的因果性。

branches.en: THE MIND: the intuition that some events cause others.
branches.cn: 心智：某些事件造成另一些事件的直觉。

intro.en: Causality is the abstract noun in -ity built on causal. The items show the same base across adjectives, nouns and compounds, including the modern research phrases.
intro.cn: causality 是建立在 causal 上的 -ity 抽象名词。下列条目展示同一词基在形容词、名词与复合词中的形态，包括现代研究短语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give cause, its adjective, and the scholastic abstract noun that English borrowed as causality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出原因、其形容词，以及英语借作 causality 的经院抽象名词。

items.meaning: the property or principle of cause and effect
items.example: The argument questions the very idea of causality.
items.exampleCN: 这一论证质疑因果性观念本身。

items.example: They looked for a causal explanation.
items.exampleCN: 他们寻找一种因果解释。

items.example: Causa is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: causa 是整个词族的词基。
经院作家使用 causalitas 一词。

items.example: The two events are causally linked.
items.exampleCN: 这两个事件有因果联系。

items.example: A causative agent produces the change.
items.exampleCN: 致因主体产生这种变化。

items.meaning: a causal direction opposite to the one assumed
items.example: Reverse causality can ruin a naive analysis.
items.exampleCN: 反向因果会毁掉一个天真的分析。

items.meaning: a simple one-way chain of causes
items.example: Complex systems rarely show linear causality.
items.exampleCN: 复杂系统很少呈现线性因果。

items.meaning: the presence of several interacting causes
items.example: Multicausality is the norm in public health.
items.exampleCN: 多因性是公共卫生中的常态。

definition_zh: 原因；起因；事业；导致；引起
definition_en: the person or thing that makes something happen, a principle that people support, or to make something happen
core_image: 推倒第一块骨牌的那只手
scene: 调查人员围着一台烧坏的机器。A loose wire was the cause of the fire.

senses.title: The reason something happens
senses.definition: the person, thing or event that makes another thing happen
senses.definitionCN: 使另一件事发生的人、物或事件
senses.example: The police are still looking for the cause of the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 警方仍在查找撞车的原因。
senses.why: The Latin word first named a legal case, then the reason behind any effect.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源词先指法律案件，后指任何结果背后的理由。

senses.title: A principle people support
senses.definition: an aim or principle that a group works for and defends
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体为之努力并捍卫的目标或原则
senses.example: She gave her life to the cause of education.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一生献给了教育事业。
senses.why: A cause worth arguing for in court becomes a cause worth working for in public life.
senses.whyCN: 值得在法庭上力争的事由，变成了值得在公共生活中奋斗的事业。

senses.title: To make something happen
senses.definition: to be the reason that an event, problem or change occurs
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事件、问题或变化发生的原因
senses.example: Heavy rain caused the river to rise.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨使河水上涨。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the noun around: to be the cause is to cause.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词反过来用：成为原因，就是去导致。

intro.en: Cause comes from a Latin word for a legal case, which widened to mean a reason and then a principle.
intro.cn: cause 来自拉丁语中表示法律案件的词，后来扩展为理由，再扩展为事业。

items.en: Causa meant a lawsuit, a plea, and also the reason behind something.
items.cn: 拉丁语 causa 指诉讼、申辩，也指某事背后的理由。

items.en: Cause kept both the legal and the explanatory senses in medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 cause 在中世纪同时保留法律义与解释义。

items.en: English cause first names a reason or motive, and the legal sense fades.
items.cn: 英语 cause 最初指理由或动机，法律义逐渐淡化。

items.en: The word extends to a principle defended in public, such as a political cause.
items.cn: 词义扩展到公共生活中所捍卫的原则，如政治事业。

items.en: Cause and effect becomes the standard phrase for the relation between events.
items.cn: cause and effect 成为表示事件关系的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the causal family, and the meaning group lists other words for reasons and sources.
note.cn: 形近组沿因果词族展开，近义组列出其他表示理由与来源的词。

entries.definition: a reason for acting in a certain way

normal.en: Cause and case both come from Latin causa, which first meant a lawsuit.
normal.cn: cause 与 case 都出自拉丁语 causa，最初指诉讼。

normal.en: Cause and effect always travel as a pair: the reason and the result.
normal.cn: cause 与 effect 总是成对出现：原因与结果。

normal.en: Because literally means by cause, which is why it answers the question why.
normal.cn: because 字面上是「由原因」，所以它回答为什么。

normal.en: Causal and causality keep the adjective and noun forms of the same idea.
normal.cn: causal 与 causality 保留了同一概念的形容词与名词形式。

normal.en: To cause something is simply to be its cause, with no change of meaning.
normal.cn: to cause 某物就是成为它的 cause，词义没有改变。

root: 源自拉丁语 causa（诉讼、理由），经古法语 cause 进入英语，由法律案件扩展为原因与事业。

sensesIntro.en: A legal case becomes a reason, a reason becomes a principle worth defending, and the verb makes the reason act.
sensesIntro.cn: 法律案件变成理由，理由变成值得捍卫的事业，动词则让这个理由发挥作用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first push that sets everything else moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：最初那一下推动，让后面的一切动起来。

branches.en: The reason sense answers the plain question why.
branches.cn: 原因义回答最朴素的「为什么」。

branches.en: A principle argued for becomes a cause people serve.
branches.cn: 被力争的原则变成了人们献身的事业。

branches.en: The verb makes the reason into an action.
branches.cn: 动词义把理由变成动作。

branches.en: Noun and verb differ only in whether the cause is named or applied.
branches.cn: 名词与动词只差在原因是被告知还是被施行。

branches.en: Both senses involve something worth standing behind.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及值得站在其后支持的东西。

intro.en: Cause builds adjectives and nouns with -al and -ality, and hides inside because.
intro.cn: cause 用 -al 与 -ality 构成形容词和名词，还藏在 because 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin causa is also the source of accuse and excuse, both built on the legal sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 causa 也是 accuse 与 excuse 的来源，两者都建立在法律义上。

definition_zh: 小心的；谨慎的；有保留的

senses.title: Careful to avoid danger

definition_zh: 停止；终止；不再存在
definition_en: to stop happening or doing something, or to come to an end

scene: 机器发出怪响，工人按下开关。The noise ceased as soon as the power was cut.

senses.title: To stop doing or happening
senses.definition: to bring or come to an end, especially of an activity or a sound
senses.definitionCN: 使活动或声音结束，或自身结束
senses.example: The rain ceased at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 雨在半夜停了。
senses.why: The Latin source meant to hold back or delay, and holding something back ends its motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是拦住或拖延，而把某物拦住就是终止它的运动。

senses.title: To stop existing
senses.definition: to come to an end as a thing that exists, often used of companies or species
senses.definitionCN: 作为存在物走到尽头，常用于公司或物种
senses.example: The old factory ceased to exist in the nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老厂在九十年代就不存在了。
senses.why: When an activity stops for ever, the thing that carried it out also stops existing.
senses.whyCN: 当一项活动永久停止，从事这项活动的事物也就不再存在。

intro.en: Cease comes from a Latin verb meaning to delay or hold back, which passed through French into English.
intro.cn: cease 来自一个意为拖延或拦住的拉丁语动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Cessare meant to be slow, to delay or to leave off an activity.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cessare 意为迟缓、拖延或停止某项活动。

items.en: Cesser carried the sense of stopping and yielding into medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 cesser 把停止与让出的含义带入中世纪法语。

items.en: Cesen appears in the fourteenth century for leaving off an action.
items.cn: 中古英语 cesen 在十四世纪已指停止某项行动。

items.en: Legal and military phrases such as cease and desist and cease fire become fixed.
items.cn: 停止并终止、停火等法律与军事说法逐渐固定。

items.en: Cease to exist extends the word from actions to the ending of things themselves.
items.cn: cease to exist 把该词从动作扩展到事物本身的终结。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the cessation family, while the meaning group lists other verbs for ending.
note.cn: 形近组沿停止词族展开，近义组列出其他表示结束的动词。

senses.title: The top surface of a room
senses.definition: the inside surface that covers the top of a room
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖房间顶部的内表面
senses.example: The ceiling is painted white.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板刷成了白色。
senses.why: The old verb meant to line or panel a room, and the panel above your head became the ceiling.
senses.whyCN: 旧动词意为给房间装衬板，头顶上那层衬板就成了天花板。

senses.title: The highest allowed level
senses.definition: the greatest amount or level that is officially allowed or possible

senses.example: The government set a ceiling on rents.
senses.exampleCN: 政府给租金设了上限。
senses.why: A ceiling is a fixed surface you cannot rise above, so any hard limit borrows the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 天花板是一层无法越过的固定平面，于是任何硬性限制都借用了这个画面。

senses.title: The height of the cloud base
senses.definition: the height above the ground at which the lowest clouds begin, used in flying

senses.example: The pilot reported a low ceiling over the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员报告海岸上空云底很低。
senses.why: To a pilot the cloud base is literally a roof over the aircraft, so the room word fits.
senses.whyCN: 对飞行员来说，云底字面上就是飞机头顶的屋顶，房间用词正好合用。

intro.cn: ceiling 来自一个意为衬里或遮盖的旧动词，与表示天空的词无关。

items.en: Celare meant to hide or conceal, and its French descendant kept that sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celare 意为隐藏或遮盖，其法语后裔保留了这个意思。

items.en: Celer meant to conceal, and also to panel or line the inside of a room.
items.cn: 古法语 celer 意为遮盖，也指给房间内侧装衬板。

items.en: Celen names the panelling of walls and roofs, especially the upper lining of a room.
items.cn: 中古英语 celen 指给墙和屋顶装衬板，尤其是房间上部的衬层。

items.en: Ceiling settles as the noun for the inner roof of a room.
items.cn: 十六世纪 ceiling 固定为指房间内侧顶面的名词。

items.en: The word spreads to price ceilings, glass ceilings and the cloud base seen by pilots.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词扩展到价格上限、无形障碍以及飞行员所见的云底。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the old verb and its adjective, while the meaning group gives other upper limits.
note.cn: 形近组保留旧动词及其形容词，近义组给出其他上部或限度说法。

entries.definition: to fit a room with a ceiling
having a ceiling of a stated kind
the outer covering on top of a building
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物顶部的外层覆盖

entries.definition: an upper limit placed on an amount
the greatest amount allowed

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the conceal root, the price phrases and the false link with sky.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用遮盖词根、价格搭配，以及与天空的错误联想。

normal.en: Ceiling and conceal share the Latin root celare, to hide, because a ceiling covers the room.
normal.cn: ceiling 与 conceal 共享拉丁语词根 celare（隐藏），因为天花板正是把房间盖住。

normal.en: The word has nothing to do with the Latin for sky, however tempting that link feels.
normal.cn: 尽管这层联想很诱人，这个词与拉丁语中表示天空的词毫无关系。

normal.en: Price ceiling and glass ceiling keep the limit sense in economics and at work.
normal.cn: price ceiling 与 glass ceiling 把上限义留在经济学与职场里。

normal.en: Hit the ceiling means explode with anger, as if your head struck the roof.
normal.cn: hit the ceiling 意思是暴怒，仿佛头撞到了屋顶。

normal.en: The plural ceilings simply adds an s to the -ing noun.
normal.cn: 复数 ceilings 只在 -ing 名词后加 s。

abstract.en: Picture a bare bulb swinging above a white plaster surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一只光灯泡在白色灰泥顶面下摆动。

abstract.en: Picture a pilot looking up at a flat grey layer of cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象飞行员抬头望见平坦的灰色云层。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing down on a rising graph line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把上升的曲线按住。

examples.en: The ceiling is too low for a tall bookshelf.
examples.cn: 天花板太低，放不下高书架。

examples.en: They put a ceiling on ticket prices.
examples.cn: 他们给票价设了上限。

examples.en: She has broken the glass ceiling in her company.
examples.cn: 她打破了公司里的无形晋升障碍。

dict_mnemonic.text: ceiling 可以想成「see 到顶」：抬头看见的那一层平面，就是天花板，也是上限。

root: 源自古法语 celer（遮盖、装衬板），上溯拉丁语 celare（隐藏），与表示天空的词无关。

sensesIntro.en: A lining that hides the roof beams becomes the room's upper surface, then any level you cannot rise above.
sensesIntro.cn: 遮住屋顶梁的衬层变成房间上部表面，再变成任何无法越过的水平线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat layer sealed over the space above your head.
core.cn: 核心意象：在头顶空间上封住的一层平面。

branches.en: The room surface keeps the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 房间顶面保留了最古老、最具体的义项。

branches.en: A limit borrows the picture of a surface you cannot pass.
branches.cn: 上限借用了无法穿过的平面这一画面。

branches.en: The cloud base becomes a roof for aircraft.
branches.cn: 云底成了飞机头顶的屋顶。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of a top that stops upward movement.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「顶端阻止上升」的意思。

branches.en: Both are technical extensions of one plain physical image.
branches.cn: 两者都是同一个具体画面在技术领域的延伸。

intro.en: Ceiling keeps the old verb ceil and a participle-like adjective, plus compounds.
intro.cn: ceiling 保留了旧动词 ceil 和类似分词的形容词，并有若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb celare, to hide, underlies the word through French celer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 celare（隐藏）经法语 celer 构成这个词的底层来源。

items.meaning: the top surface of a room

items.example: The two rooms have high ceilings.
items.exampleCN: 两个房间的天花板都很高。

items.example: They ceiled the hall in oak.
items.exampleCN: 他们用橡木给大厅装了顶。

items.meaning: having a ceiling of a kind

items.meaning: a fan fixed to the ceiling
items.meaningCN: 固定在天花板上的风扇

items.meaning: a lamp fixed to the ceiling
a legal upper limit on prices

items.exampleCN: 价格上限让小商店受了损。

items.example: Celare is the deep root of ceiling.
items.exampleCN: celare 是 ceiling 的深层词根。

latinEntries.example: Celare passed into French as celer.
latinEntries.exampleCN: celare 传入法语成为 celer。

definition_zh: 庆祝；庆贺；赞颂；主持（仪式）
definition_en: to do something enjoyable to mark a special occasion, to praise someone publicly, or to perform a religious ceremony
core_image: 人群聚在一起，为一件好事高声欢呼
scene: 球队赢下决赛的当晚，整条街都很热闹。The whole street came out to celebrate the victory.
sceneCN: 这里 celebrate 指「庆祝」（第 1 个义项：用热闹活动纪念喜事）；句意是整条街的人都出来庆祝这场胜利。

senses.title: To mark a happy occasion
senses.definition: to do something enjoyable in order to mark a special day or event
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念特别的日子或事件而做些令人愉快的事
senses.example: We celebrated her graduation with a dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们用一顿晚饭庆祝她毕业。
senses.why: A crowded gathering on a feast day is the oldest picture behind the word, and joy is still its centre.
senses.whyCN: 节日里人群聚集是这个词最古老的画面，而喜悦至今仍是它的中心。

senses.title: To praise someone publicly
senses.definition: to speak or write about someone's achievements with approval
senses.definitionCN: 带着赞许谈论或书写某人的成就
senses.example: The poem celebrates the courage of ordinary workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗赞颂普通工人的勇气。
senses.why: Public honour grows from public festivity: the crowd that gathers to rejoice can also gather to praise.
senses.whyCN: 公开的荣誉源自公开的欢庆：为高兴而聚集的人群，也能为赞美而聚集。

senses.title: To perform a religious ceremony
senses.definition: to lead or perform a formal religious rite such as Mass
senses.definitionCN: 主持弥撒等正式宗教仪式
senses.example: The priest celebrated Mass at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 神父在黎明主持了弥撒。
senses.why: Church ritual is a solemn gathering, so the verb for gathering to honour extends to conducting the rite.
senses.whyCN: 教会仪式是庄严的聚集，于是表示聚集致敬的动词也扩展到主持仪式。

intro.en: Celebrate comes from a Latin verb for honouring in a crowd, built on an adjective meaning crowded or famous.
intro.cn: celebrate 来自拉丁语中在人前致敬的动词，其词基是一个意为拥挤或著名的形容词。

items.en: Celeber meant crowded, busy or well known.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celeber 意为拥挤、繁忙或著名的。

items.en: Celebrare meant to gather in numbers and to honour someone publicly.
items.cn: celebrare 意为众人聚集，并公开向某人致敬。

items.en: English celebrate first appears in religious use, for performing a rite.
items.cn: 英语 celebrate 最早见于宗教用法，指举行仪式。

items.en: The word widens to feasting and merrymaking on special days.
items.cn: 词义扩展到在特别的日子里宴饮欢庆。

items.en: Modern usage adds the sense of praising a person or idea in art and writing.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上在艺术与文字中赞颂人物或观念的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the celebration family, while the meaning group lists other words for marking and honouring.
note.cn: 形近组沿庆祝词族展开，近义组列出其他表示纪念与致敬的词。

entries.definition: a party or event that marks something
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念某事而办的聚会或活动

entries.definition: a famous person, or the state of being famous
expressing joy at a special event
entries.definitionCN: 为特别事件表达喜悦的

entries.definition: to remember and honour a person or event formally
entries.definitionCN: 正式纪念并致敬某人或某事

entries.definition: to feel or show great joy
entries.definitionCN: 感到或表现出极大喜悦

entries.definition: to show respect or praise publicly

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie celebrate to the crowded root, to celebration and to the fixed occasion phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 celebrate 与拥挤词根、celebration 以及固定场合搭配连起来。

normal.en: The Latin root celeber meant crowded, so to celebrate is to fill a place with people who care.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 celeber 意为拥挤，所以庆祝就是让在乎的人把地方填满。

normal.en: Celebration, celebrity and celebratory all keep the same -celebr- stem.
normal.cn: celebration、celebrity、celebratory 都保留同一个 -celebr- 词干。

normal.en: A celebrity is literally a much-celebrated person, one whose name is spoken everywhere.
normal.cn: celebrity 字面上就是被大家广泛称颂的人，名字到处被提起。

normal.en: Celebrate a birthday and celebrate success fix the joyful sense in daily life.
normal.cn: celebrate a birthday 与 celebrate success 把喜悦义固定在日常生活里。

normal.en: Celebrate Mass shows the older, religious sense surviving in church language.
normal.cn: celebrate Mass 显示较古老、宗教性的义项仍活在教会用语里。

abstract.en: Picture a street full of shouting people after a final whistle.
abstract.cn: 想象终场哨响后满街欢呼的人群。

abstract.en: Picture a raised glass and a table covered with dishes.
abstract.cn: 想象举起的酒杯和一桌菜肴。

abstract.en: Picture a choir singing under a high stone roof.
abstract.cn: 想象唱诗班在高大的石顶下歌唱。

examples.en: They celebrated their anniversary with a quiet trip.
examples.cn: 他们用一次安静的旅行庆祝结婚纪念日。

examples.en: The whole town celebrates the harvest each autumn.
examples.cn: 全镇每年秋天都庆祝丰收。

examples.en: The book celebrates the lives of ordinary people.
examples.cn: 这本书赞颂普通人的生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: celebrate 里有 celebr：把它想成「塞勒布雷特」节的欢呼，人一聚齐，庆祝就开始了。

root: 源自拉丁语 celebrare（聚集致敬），词基 celeber 意为拥挤、著名，经中古英语进入宗教与日常用法。

sensesIntro.en: A crowded feast gives joyful celebration, public praise grows from the same crowd, and church ritual keeps the solemn side.
sensesIntro.cn: 人群聚集的宴饮给出欢庆，公开赞美从同一人群生长，教会仪式则保留庄严的一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd gathered to honour one happy event.
core.cn: 核心意象：为一件喜事聚在一起的人群。

branches.en: The joyful feast is the sense most people use today.
branches.cn: 欢庆宴饮是今天最多人使用的义项。

branches.en: Public honour turns the crowd toward praise rather than party.
branches.cn: 公开荣誉把人群从聚会转向赞美。

branches.en: Religious ritual keeps the formal, gathered side of the word.
branches.cn: 宗教仪式保留了该词正式、聚集的一面。

branches.en: Both are ceremonies, one joyful and one solemn.
branches.cn: 两者都是仪式，一个欢快，一个庄严。

branches.en: Both put a person or event at the centre of public attention.
branches.cn: 两者都把人物或事件放在公众注意的中心。

intro.en: Celebrate builds nouns and adjectives with -ion, -ity and -ory, all on the same stem.
intro.cn: celebrate 用 -ion、-ity、-ory 在同一词干上构成名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base celeber, crowded or famous, also survives in celebrity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 celeber（拥挤或著名）也活在 celebrity 里。

definition_zh: n. 名人，名流；名声，名气
definition_en: a famous person; the state of being famous
core_image: 闪光灯围住一张熟悉的脸
scene: 闪光灯一亮，这位名人在红毯上停下脚步。The celebrity paused on the red carpet as the cameras flashed.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：celebrity 指名人；句意是名人在红毯上被闪光灯围住。

senses.title: A famous person
senses.definition: a person who is well known to the public
senses.definitionCN: 为公众熟知的人
senses.example: The restaurant is popular with celebrities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅很受名人欢迎。
senses.why: The word came from Latin celeber, crowded or famous.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自拉丁语 celeber（热闹的、著名的）。

senses.title: The state of being famous
senses.definition: the condition of being widely known
senses.definitionCN: 被广泛知晓的状态
senses.example: The film brought her sudden celebrity.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影让她一夜成名。
senses.why: The abstract sense came before the person sense.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义先于名人义出现。

intro.en: Celebrity comes from Latin celebritas, fame, from celeber, crowded or well known.
intro.cn: celebrity 源自拉丁语 celebritas（名声），来自 celeber（热闹的、著名的）。

items.en: Latin celeber means crowded or famous.

items.en: Celebritas names fame.

items.en: English celebrity first means a solemn rite.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语最初指庄严仪式。

items.en: The word settles into the sense of fame.
items.cn: 十七世纪固定为名声义。

items.en: Film and television create modern celebrities.
items.cn: 二十世纪影视造就现代名人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the celebr- stem; the near-meaning group separates fame from the famous person.
note.cn: 形近组共享 celebr- 词干；近义组区分名声与名人。

sensesIntro.en: Fame came first as a word, and then it named the people who carry it.

definition_zh: n. 芹菜

definition_zh: 天空的；天体的；天国的；文学用语中表示「超凡的、极美的」
definition_en: relating to the sky, to the bodies in it, or to heaven, especially in astronomy and religious writing
core_image: 夜里抬头，满天光点像钉在一张深蓝色穹顶上，地面之上的一切都挂在这张穹顶下面
scene: 天文台圆顶打开后，观测者把镜筒对准一片星群，记录它们缓慢移动的位置。The celestial map on the wall showed where each star would rise.
sceneCN: 这里 celestial 指「属于天空的、天上的」（第 1 个义项：与天空或天体有关）；句意为墙上的星空图显示了每颗星将从何处升起。图中可辨识物件：星空图、望远镜、圆顶、赤道仪。

pos.zh: 文学用法：超凡的；极美的

derivatives.zh: 天青石（以天空命名的锶矿物）
天青石的别名；亦用作颜色名

senses.title: Of the sky as a vault
senses.definition: belonging to the sky as seen from the earth, especially the vault in which the stars appear
senses.definitionCN: 属于从地面所见的天空，尤指星星所在的那层穹顶
senses.example: Ancient sailors read the celestial vault the way we read a map.
senses.exampleCN: 古代水手像我们读地图一样读那片天穹。
senses.why: caelum named the sky itself, so the adjective first describes anything that belongs to that vault.
senses.whyCN: caelum 本指天空本身，因此这个形容词最初描述一切属于那层穹顶的事物。

senses.title: Of a heavenly body
senses.definition: relating to a star, planet, moon or other object in space rather than to the earth
senses.definitionCN: 与恒星、行星、卫星等太空中的物体有关，而非与地球有关
senses.example: Celestial objects were charted long before their distances were known.
senses.exampleCN: 早在测出距离之前，天体就被绘制成图了。
senses.why: once the sky was filled with named bodies, the adjective naturally followed them.
senses.whyCN: 当天空被逐一命名出各种天体之后，这个形容词自然就跟着这些天体走了。

senses.title: Of heaven or the divine
senses.definition: belonging to heaven or to divine beings, especially in religious writing
senses.definitionCN: 属于天国或神灵，尤见于宗教文字
senses.example: The hymn describes a celestial choir that never rests.
senses.exampleCN: 这首赞美诗描绘了一支永不休止的天国合唱队。
senses.why: Latin caelum covered both the visible sky and the home of the gods, so the adjective kept both readings.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 caelum 既指可见的天空，也指众神的居所，因此这个形容词同时保留了这两层意思。

senses.title: Blissfully beautiful
senses.definition: so beautiful or blissful that it seems to belong to another world
senses.definitionCN: 美得像不属于这个世界，或幸福得如同身处另一世界
senses.example: The soprano's celestial tone silenced the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 女高音那种超凡的音色让全场安静下来。
senses.why: the religious sense softened into a word for beauty that seems not to be of this earth.
senses.whyCN: 宗教义逐渐柔化，转指仿佛不属于人间的美。

senses.title: Of a star map or globe
senses.definition: relating to a map or globe that represents the sky as a surface
senses.definitionCN: 与把天空画成一个曲面的星图或天球仪有关
senses.example: A celestial globe shows the constellations as they look from the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 天球仪显示出从地球看去的各个星座。
senses.why: instruments that picture the sky borrow the adjective, because they draw the vault as a surface.
senses.whyCN: 把天空画成图面的仪器借用了这个形容词，因为它们把那层穹顶画成了一个曲面。

senses.title: Of navigation by the stars
senses.definition: using the positions of stars and other bodies to find one's way
senses.definitionCN: 利用恒星等天体的位置来确定方位
senses.example: Celestial navigation needs a clear horizon and an accurate clock.
senses.exampleCN: 天文导航需要清晰的地平线和准确的时钟。
senses.why: sailors measured the sky to locate themselves, and the fixed phrase kept the adjective in everyday technical use.
senses.whyCN: 水手通过测量天空来确定自己的位置，这一固定说法把这个形容词留在了日常技术语中。

senses.title: Of the mechanics of bodies
senses.definition: relating to the calculated motions and mutual pulls of bodies in space
senses.definitionCN: 与太空中天体的运动及其相互引力计算有关
senses.example: Celestial mechanics predicts the slow drift of the moon's orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 天体力学预测月球轨道的缓慢漂移。
senses.why: mathematical study of the sky turned the adjective into a technical label for motion under gravity.
senses.whyCN: 对天空的数学研究把这个形容词变成了描述引力下运动的技术标签。

senses.title: Detached from earthly matters
senses.definition: figurative: free of ordinary earthly concerns, almost otherworldly
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：摆脱世俗牵挂，近乎不属于人间
senses.example: He kept a celestial calm while the room argued around him.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里众人争吵，他却保持着一种超脱的平静。
senses.why: if heaven is above the earth, a mood can also be lifted clear of earthly noise.
senses.whyCN: 既然天在人间之上，一种心境自然也能被托离尘世的喧闹。

intro.en: Celestial comes through Medieval Latin and Old French from Latin caelestis 'of the sky, heavenly', built on caelum 'sky, heaven'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: celestial 经中世纪拉丁语与古法语进入英语，来自拉丁 caelestis「天空的、天上的」，词根为 caelum「天空、天」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caelum meant 'sky, heaven', and was also used for 'climate, region'. A separate caelum meaning 'chisel' exists; whether the two are one word is disputed, so they should not be assumed to be related.
items.cn: caelum 意为「天空、天」，也用于指「气候、地区」。另有一个 caelum 意为「凿子」；两者是否同为一个词尚有争议，不能直接假定同源。

items.en: The adjective caelestis 'heavenly, of the sky' was formed on caelum and used of gods, stars and the heavens.
items.cn: 形容词 caelestis「天上的、天空的」由 caelum 构成，用于神灵、星辰与天界。

items.en: Medieval Latin celestialis and Old French celestial carried the adjective into English in the late fourteenth century, first in religious texts.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 celestialis 与古法语 celestial 在十四世纪末把这个形容词带入英语，最初见于宗教文本。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word was applied to the geometry of the sky, giving fixed phrases such as celestial sphere and celestial mechanics.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个词被用于描述天空的几何，形成天球、天体力学等固定说法。

items.en: The older religious sense survived in literary writing for anything blissful or supremely beautiful.
items.cn: 较早的宗教义在文学中保留下来，用来形容幸福至极或美到极点的东西。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin origin of caelum is not established, and suggested links to the 'chisel' word or to a reconstructed Italic form remain hypotheses. The earliest English citation is usually placed in the late fourteenth century but is not exact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：caelum 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明，把它与「凿子」义或某个重构的意大利语族形式相联系仍属假说。英语最早书证通常放在十四世纪末，但并不确切。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the letters cel- but come from unrelated Latin roots; group two holds words that really do describe the sky or the divine.
note.cn: 第一组是同样以 cel- 开头、却来自不同拉丁词根的词；第二组才是真正表示天空或神圣事物的近义词。

entries.definition: From Latin celebrare and celeber 'frequented, famous', not from caelum: to mark an occasion with ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 celebrare 与 celeber「常有人来的、著名的」，并非出自 caelum：以仪式庆祝某件事。

entries.definition: From Latin caelebs 'unmarried', a different root: abstaining from marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 caelebs「未婚的」，词根不同：不婚的。

entries.definition: From Latin cellarium 'store-room', from cella 'room': an underground room for storing things.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cellarium「储藏室」，源于 cella「房间」：存放物品的地下室。

entries.definition: From Latin celer 'swift': speed. The shared letters with celestial are coincidence.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 celer「迅捷的」：迅速。与 celestial 相同的字母只是巧合。

entries.definition: The ordinary adjective for the sky or for heaven; celestial is its learned equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 指天空或天国的日常形容词；celestial 是它带学术气质的对应词。

entries.definition: Relating to astronomy or to the objects it studies; it carries no religious overtone.
entries.definitionCN: 与天文学或天文学研究的对象有关；不带宗教色彩。

entries.definition: Belonging to a god or godlike; celestial means this only in religious or literary use.
entries.definitionCN: 属于神或如神一般；celestial 只在宗教或文学用法中才有这层意思。

entries.definition: Light, airy, as if made of the upper air; celestial is more often about position than texture.
entries.definitionCN: 轻盈飘渺，仿佛由高层空气构成；celestial 更多讲位置，而非质地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: caelum 'sky' plus the relational suffix -ial: the adjective of the sky.
normal.cn: caelum「天空」加上关系形容词后缀 -ial：属于天空的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs celestial, celestially, celestite and celestine.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 celestial、celestially、celestite 与 celestine。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: celestial body, celestial mechanics, celestial navigation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：天体、天体力学、天文导航。

normal.en: The same relational ending builds terrestrial and aerial, both adjectives of position.
normal.cn: 同一关系后缀还构成 terrestrial 与 aerial，两者都是表示位置的形容词。

normal.en: Star charts and sextants keep the word at sea and in the observatory.
normal.cn: 星图与六分仪把这个词留在海上和天文台里。

abstract.en: Picture a dome of small lamps switched on above a dark field.
abstract.cn: 想象一片暗地上方点亮一圈小灯，罩成一个穹顶。

abstract.en: Picture a choir heard through a thick stone wall, beautiful and far away.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着一堵厚石墙听见合唱，美好而遥远。

abstract.en: Picture a person so calm that the weather seems to stop at their shoulders.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人静得让天气都在他肩头停住。

examples.en: The celestial sphere is a model, not a real object.
examples.cn: 天球只是一个模型，并非真实存在的物体。

examples.en: Celestial navigation guided the ship across the Pacific.
examples.cn: 天文导航引导这艘船横渡太平洋。

examples.en: The cathedral ceiling was painted to look like a celestial realm.
examples.cn: 教堂穹顶被画成天界的模样。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把天空当作一张穹顶：抬头所见的光点，全都属于这张穹顶 → 天空的、天体的、天上的

root: 拉丁 caelum「天空、天」→ caelestis「天空的、天上的」→ 中世纪拉丁 celestialis → 英语 celestial；caelum 更深来源不确定，与「凿子」义的 caelum 是否同词尚有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one upward look: the vault of the sky, the bodies inside it, the heaven beyond it, the beauty that seems to come from there, the instruments that map it, and finally the calm of someone lifted above the earth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次抬头展开：先看天空的穹顶，再看其中的天体，然后是穹顶之外的天国、仿佛来自那里的美、描绘天空的仪器，最后是一个仿佛被托离尘世的人所带的平静。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark dome pricked with points of light, with everything above the ground hanging from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：深色穹顶上布满光点，地面之上的一切都挂在这张穹顶底下。

branches.en: THE VAULT AND ITS MAP: the sky treated as a surface, and the instruments that draw that surface.
branches.cn: 穹顶与图：把天空当作一个曲面，以及描绘这个曲面的仪器。

branches.en: BODIES AND THEIR PATHS: objects in space, the routes found by watching them, and the mathematics of those routes.
branches.cn: 天体与路径：太空中的物体、靠观测找到的路线，以及这些路线的数学。

branches.en: HEAVEN: the same word serves the sky of religion as well as the sky of astronomy.
branches.cn: 天国：同一个词既服务天文学的天空，也服务宗教的天空。

branches.en: BEAUTY: what seems to come from above is felt as perfection.
branches.cn: 美：仿佛来自上方的东西，被人感受为完美。

branches.en: DETACHMENT: a person can be lifted clear of earthly noise, as if into another layer.
branches.cn: 超脱：一个人可以被托离尘世喧闹，仿佛升入另一层。

intro.en: Celestial is a Latin adjective whose root and relational suffix also build a small family, so the word can be read in pieces.
intro.cn: celestial 是一个拉丁形容词，其词根与关系后缀还构成一个小词族，因此可以按语素逐块读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin caelum gives celestial and the mineral name celestite, while the English relational suffix -ial marks an adjective of belonging.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 caelum 衍生 celestial 与矿物名 celestite，英语关系后缀 -ial 则表示「属于……的」形容词。

items.example: Caelum also named a region or climate in Latin geography.
items.exampleCN: 在拉丁地理学中，caelum 也指地区或气候带。

items.example: Caelestis was used of stars, gods and the heavens.
items.exampleCN: caelestis 用于星辰、神灵与天界。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.meaning: of the sky or of heaven
items.example: The celestial map hung above the telescope.
items.exampleCN: 星空图挂在望远镜上方。

items.meaningCN: 以天空般的方式；超凡地

items.meaning: strontium sulphate, named for its pale blue colour
items.meaningCN: 天青石，硫酸锶矿物，因淡蓝色而得名
items.exampleCN: 天青石晶体衬满这个晶洞。

items.meaning: an imaginary sphere on which the stars are projected
items.meaningCN: 把星星投影其上的假想天球
items.example: Astronomers still use the celestial sphere as a coordinate model.
items.exampleCN: 天文学家仍把天球当作坐标模型使用。

items.meaning: the mathematical study of orbital motion
items.meaningCN: 研究轨道运动的数学分支
items.example: Celestial mechanics explains the tides and the seasons.
items.exampleCN: 天体力学解释潮汐与季节。

definition_zh: 细胞；小室；牢房；电池
definition_en: the smallest living unit of an animal or plant, a small room such as a prison room, or a device that stores electric power
core_image: 一个四面封闭的小格子
scene: 显微镜下能看到微小的结构。Each cell in the sample had a dark centre.
sceneCN: 这里 cell 指「细胞」（第 1 个义项：生物体最小的生命单位）；句意是样本里的每个细胞都有一个深色的中心。

senses.title: The basic unit of life
senses.definition: the smallest part of a living thing that can carry out the processes of life
senses.definitionCN: 生物体中能进行生命活动的最小单位
senses.example: A red blood cell carries oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 红细胞负责运送氧气。
senses.why: Early microscopists saw tiny walled compartments and borrowed the word for a small room.
senses.whyCN: 早期显微镜学家看到一个个有壁的小隔间，就借用了表示小房间的词。

senses.title: A small closed room
senses.definition: a small room, especially one in a prison or a monastery
senses.definitionCN: 小型房间，尤指监狱或修道院中的
senses.example: The prisoner paced his narrow cell.
senses.exampleCN: 犯人在狭窄的牢房里来回踱步。
senses.why: This is the original sense: a small enclosed room, from Latin cella.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：拉丁语 cella 所指的小型封闭房间。

senses.title: A unit that stores electric power
senses.definition: a container of chemicals that produces electricity, or one unit of a larger battery
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学物质产生电的容器，或电池组中的一节
senses.example: The torch needs a new cell.
senses.exampleCN: 手电筒需要换一节电池。
senses.why: Each battery unit is a sealed compartment, so the room word fits the small power box.
senses.whyCN: 每个电池单元都是密封的小格，于是房间用词正好套在这只电源小盒上。

intro.en: Cell comes from Latin cella, a small room, and every later sense keeps the idea of a closed compartment.
intro.cn: cell 来自拉丁语 cella（小房间），后面每个义项都保留封闭小格的意思。

items.en: Cella meant a small room, a storeroom or a shrine chamber.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cella 指小房间、储藏室或神庙内室。

items.en: Celle named a small room, especially a monk's chamber.
items.cn: 古法语 celle 指小房间，尤指修士的居室。

items.en: Cell covers small rooms in monasteries and prisons.
items.cn: 中古英语 cell 涵盖修道院和监狱的小室。

items.en: Microscopy applies the word to the tiny compartments seen in living tissue.
items.cn: 十七世纪显微镜学把该词用到活体组织中的微小隔间上。

items.en: Electricity adds the battery sense, and compounds such as cell phone spread the word further.
items.cn: 电学又添上电池义，cell phone 等复合词进一步推广该词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the room root through its derivatives, while the meaning group lists other enclosed spaces.
note.cn: 形近组沿房间词根经派生词展开，近义组列出其他封闭空间。

entries.definition: made of cells, or relating to mobile phones
entries.definitionCN: 由细胞组成的，或与移动电话有关的

entries.definition: a person who shares a prison cell
the substance forming plant cell walls
entries.definitionCN: 构成植物细胞壁的物质

entries.definition: a part of a building enclosed by walls
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物中被墙围起的一部分

entries.definition: a large room used for a special purpose
entries.definitionCN: 用于特定用途的大房间

entries.definition: one of several separate sections
entries.definitionCN: 若干分隔部分中的一格

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the little-room root, the blood and prison phrases and the -ular ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用小房间词根、血液与监狱搭配以及 -ular 词尾。

normal.en: Cell is simply Latin cella, a small room, and every sense is still a little box.
normal.cn: cell 就是拉丁语 cella（小房间），每个义项都还是一个小盒子。

normal.en: A prison cell and a biological cell share one shape: a wall around a small space.
normal.cn: 牢房与生物细胞共享一个形状：围住小空间的墙。

normal.en: Cellular means made of cells, and also names the mobile phone network built from small areas.
normal.cn: cellular 意为由细胞组成，也指由小区域构成的移动电话网。

normal.en: Cellmate is cell plus mate, the person sharing that small room.
normal.cn: cellmate 是 cell 加 mate，同住那间小室的人。

normal.en: The plural cells is regular, and the word stays one syllable throughout.
normal.cn: 复数 cells 变化规则，整词始终只有一个音节。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny walled box seen through a microscope lens.
abstract.cn: 想象透过显微镜镜片看到的一个微小带壁盒子。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow stone room with one high window.
abstract.cn: 想象一间窄小的石屋，只有一扇高窗。

abstract.en: Picture a small metal cylinder sliding into a torch.
abstract.cn: 想象一节小金属筒滑进手电筒。

examples.en: The disease attacks healthy cells in the blood.
examples.cn: 这种病攻击血液中的健康细胞。

examples.en: He spent three nights in a police cell.
examples.cn: 他在警局牢房里待了三晚。

examples.en: This lamp runs on a single cell.
examples.cn: 这盏灯只用一节电池。

dict_mnemonic.text: cell 读音短促，像把小盒子「塞」进口袋：细胞、牢房、电池都是一个个封闭的小格。

root: 源自拉丁语 cella（小房间、储藏室），经古法语 celle 进入英语，由房间义扩展到生物细胞与电池单元。

sensesIntro.en: A small room gives the prison sense, the microscope borrows the shape for life, and electricity borrows it again for power units.
sensesIntro.cn: 小房间给出牢房义，显微镜借这个形状指生命单位，电学又借它指电源单元。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small space shut in by walls.
core.cn: 核心意象：四面被墙围住的小空间。

branches.en: Monastery and prison rooms keep the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 修道院与监狱的房间保留最古老的义项。

branches.en: Microscopy transfers the walled box to living tissue.
branches.cn: 显微镜学把带壁盒子转移到活体组织上。

branches.en: Electricity seals chemicals inside a small cylinder.
branches.cn: 电学把化学物质封在小圆筒里。

branches.en: Both are tiny enclosed units separated from neighbours.
branches.cn: 两者都是与邻居隔开的小封闭单元。

branches.en: Both senses keep the physical container visible.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了可见的实体容器。

intro.en: Cell builds adjectives and nouns with -ular, -ulose and the compound mate.
intro.cn: cell 用 -ular、-ulose 以及复合成分 mate 构成形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cella also gives cellar and the first element of cemetery.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cella 也给出 cellar，以及 cemetery 的前半部分。

items.meaning: a small room or living unit

items.example: His cellmate taught him to read.
Her cell phone rang in the meeting.
The prison cell had no window.
Cella is the source of cell.
items.exampleCN: cella 是 cell 的来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cella 也是 cellar 的来源。

definition_zh: n. 地窖，地下室；酒窖
definition_en: a room under a house, often used for storage; a store of wine
core_image: 木楼梯通向堆满酒瓶的阴凉地窖
scene: 他提着灯走下木楼梯，地窖里堆着一排排酒瓶。He carried a lamp down to the cellar, where rows of bottles were stored.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cellar 指地窖；句意是他提灯下到堆满酒瓶的地窖。

senses.title: The room under a house
senses.definition: a room below ground level, usually under a house
senses.definitionCN: 通常位于房屋下方的地下房间
senses.example: The potatoes were kept in the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 土豆存放在地窖里。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin cellarium, a store room.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自拉丁语 cellarium（储藏室）。

senses.title: A wine store
senses.definition: a collection or store of wine, often in such a room
senses.definitionCN: 常存于此类房间中的一批酒或酒库
senses.example: The restaurant has an excellent cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅的酒窖很棒。
senses.why: Wine storage made the room stand for its contents.
senses.whyCN: 储酒让房间名也代表了所储之物。

intro.en: Cellar comes from Latin cellarium, a store room, from cella, a small room.
intro.cn: cellar 源自拉丁语 cellarium（储藏室），来自 cella（小室）。

items.en: Latin cella means a small room.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cella 意为小室。

items.en: Cellarium names a store room.
items.cn: cellarium 指储藏室。

items.en: English celler names an underground store.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语指地下储藏室。

items.en: Country houses keep wine cellars.
items.cn: 十七世纪乡间宅邸设酒窖。

items.en: A cellar can mean a wine collection.
items.cn: 现代也能指藏酒。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cel- start; the near-meaning group sorts rooms below and above ground.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cel- 开头；近义组区分地下与地上房间。

entries.definition: The basic unit of living things.
A person who sells goods.
Made of or relating to cells.
A floor below ground level.
A secure room for valuables.
A room under the roof.

normalIntro.en: A cellar is a small room that went underground.
normalIntro.cn: cellar 是搬到地下的小房间。

normal.en: Cella meant a small room.
normal.cn: cella 意为小室。

normal.en: A cellar stores food under a house.
normal.cn: 地窖在房子下面储藏食物。

normal.en: Cool earth keeps wine steady.
normal.cn: 凉爽的泥土让酒保持稳定。

normal.en: A wine cellar can mean the wine itself.
normal.cn: 酒窖也可指藏酒。

normal.en: The word is close to cell.
normal.cn: 这个词与 cell 相近。

abstract.en: A house keeping a secret below.
abstract.cn: 房子在下面藏着一个秘密。

abstract.en: Cool darkness for slow bottles.
abstract.cn: 给慢熟的酒准备的凉暗处。

abstract.en: A room where the earth is the wall.
abstract.cn: 泥土就是墙的房间。

examples.en: They stored apples and potatoes in the cellar.
examples.cn: 他们把苹果和土豆存放在地窖里。

examples.en: The hotel boasts a cellar of rare wines.
examples.cn: 这家酒店以珍藏名贵葡萄酒的酒窖自豪。

examples.en: The old inn has two cellars beneath the kitchen.
examples.cn: 这家老客栈厨房下方有两个地窖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞勒」——把东西塞进地下的小屋，就是地窖。

root: 拉丁语 cella（小室）→ cellarium（储藏室）→ 英语 cellar

sensesIntro.en: The room and the wine share a name because the room was built for the wine.
sensesIntro.cn: 房间与酒共名，因为房间本为酒而建。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp moving past dusty bottles underground
core.cn: 核心意象：灯从地下积灰的酒瓶旁移过

branches.en: Sacks of potatoes in the dark.
branches.cn: 黑暗中一袋袋土豆。

branches.en: A wooden stair down from the kitchen.
branches.cn: 厨房通下的木楼梯。

branches.en: Racks of dusty bottles.
branches.cn: 一排排积灰的酒瓶。

branches.en: A list of rare vintages.
branches.cn: 一张名贵年份酒单。

branches.en: A cool room full of time.
branches.cn: 装满时间的凉爽房间。

intro.en: Cellar has a Latin root; the list below adds words for rooms, storing and wine.
intro.cn: cellar 有拉丁词根；下面列出房间、储藏、酒词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cella is a small room, and vinum is wine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cella 意为小室，vinum 意为葡萄酒。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cella 产生 cellar 与 cell。
vinum 产生 vine 与 vinegar。
crypta 产生 crypt 与 cryptic。
